mainTopic: Work on ערב פסח and חול המועד: finishing versus starting, permitted crafts, hens, dung, vessels at the craftsman, and the customs of יריחו
overview: This amud discusses what work is allowed on ערב פסח, the fourteenth of ניסן. First, the גמרא finishes a ברייתא and decides that its real point is 'finish yes, start no.' It then proves from רבי מאיר that work for the festival is allowed and other work is not. Next, it explains the חכמים, who allow tailors, barbers and launderers to work. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds shoemakers, and the two sides disagree whether we learn starting work from finishing work. A new משנה allows setting hens on eggs, clearing dung, and taking vessels to and from a craftsman. The גמרא explains these rules using the difference between ערב פסח and חול המועד. Along the way it brings an argument between רב הונא and רבי אמי about big and small losses. Finally, a new משנה begins listing six customs of the people of יריחו, and that list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: finish what you started, but do not start anything new
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא already under discussion concludes: work begun before the fourteenth may be finished on the fourteenth. Work not begun before then may not be started, even something tiny.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may finish it on the fourteenth. When is that true? When he started it before the fourteenth. But if he did not start it before the fourteenth, he may not start it on the fourteenth, not even a small belt or a small hairnet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא it is using to answer its question about work on ערב פסח. The ברייתא allows finishing work on the fourteenth but forbids starting new work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא draws a line between work that was already started and brand-new work. The words 'even a small belt, even a small hairnet' show that starting is forbidden no matter how small the project is. The next step will try to learn something more from the ברייתא's wording.

phrases.english: one finishes it on the fourteenth,
When is that true?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִתְחִיל בָּהּ קוֹדֶם אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר,
phrases.english: when he started it before the fourteenth.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא הִתְחִיל בָּהּ קוֹדֶם אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר —
phrases.english: But if he did not start it before the fourteenth,
he may not start it on the fourteenth,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ צִילְצוֹל קָטָן, אֲפִילּוּ שְׂבָכָה קְטַנָּה.
phrases.english: not even a small belt, not even a small hairnet.
phrases.notes: Even the smallest new project may not be started.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא quoted on the previous amud as a possible answer to the בעיא about work on ערב פסח.
steps.raayaObject: The open question about which kinds of work are allowed on ערב פסח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that allows finishing work on the fourteenth but forbids starting it.

steps.title: Inference: only work for the festival may be finished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely and infers that finishing is allowed only when the work is for the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the needs of the festival, yes. Not for the needs of the festival, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא: because it spoke about festival work, only festival work may be finished. Other work may not be finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא hopes this inference answers its question, showing that the deciding factor is whether the work is for the festival. This proposed reading is challenged in the very next step.

keyTerms.meaning: for the needs of the festival

phrases.english: For the needs of the festival, yes;
not for the needs of the festival, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְצוֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד — אִין, שֶׁלֹּא לְצוֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the line on ערב פסח depends on whether the work is for the festival.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's wording about festival work.

steps.title: Rejection: the ברייתא's real point is finishing versus starting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. Even non-festival work may be finished. The ברייתא's חידוש is that even festival work may only be finished, not started.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true even for work that is not for the festival; we may finish that too. What the ברייתא is teaching us is that even for the festival, finishing is allowed and starting is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 2. The ברייתא was not limiting finishing to festival work. Its point was that even festival work may not be started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mentioned festival work to make a bigger point, not to exclude other work. Even with the strongest reason to allow work, the festival, starting is still forbidden. So the ברייתא supports the view that the dividing line is finishing versus starting, and the proof for the other view falls away.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that mentioning 'festival needs' means non-festival work is forbidden. Here the גמרא says the ברייתא picked the strongest case to teach that starting is forbidden even then.

phrases.english: The same law applies,
that even when it is not for the festival, we also finish it;
and this is what it teaches us:
that even for the needs of the festival,
finishing, yes; starting, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְצוֹרֶךְ נָמֵי גָּמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא limits finishing to festival work.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא mentioned festival work as the strongest case, to show that starting is forbidden even then. It did not mean to exclude non-festival work from finishing.

steps.title: A new proof from רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: רבי מאיר says festival work may be finished on the fourteenth and non-festival work is forbidden. He adds that work is done until midday where that is the custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי מאיר says, any work that is for the festival may be finished on the fourteenth, and work that is not for the festival is forbidden. And people do work on ערב פסח until midday in a place where that is the custom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to answer its question by quoting a ברייתא from רבי מאיר. This step sets up the source, and the next step draws the lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי מאיר says openly that non-festival work is forbidden. That is stronger than the previous ברייתא, where the festival limit was only inferred. His second clause, about local custom, is the part the גמרא will analyze.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Meir says:
Any work that is for the needs of the festival,
one may finish it on the fourteenth;
and work that is not for the festival is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה בְּעַרְבֵי פְסָחִים עַד חֲצוֹת
phrases.english: And people do work on the eves of Pesach until midday
in a place where they are accustomed to do so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא brings a different source.
steps.raayaObject: Which work is allowed on ערב פסח.

steps.title: Drawing the lesson: festival work yes, other work no
steps.stepSummary: From the custom clause, the גמרא infers that where there is no custom, work is not allowed. Taking רבי מאיר's ruling as a whole, it concludes that festival work is allowed and non-festival work is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a place where they are accustomed, yes. Where they are not accustomed, no. And learn from it: for the needs of the festival, yes; not for the needs of the festival, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רבי מאיר's words closely to answer its question. It concludes that the deciding factor on ערב פסח is whether the work is for the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The custom clause shows that work on ערב פסח is not automatically allowed everywhere. Together with רבי מאיר's first clause, the permitted category is festival work, and non-festival work stays forbidden. This answers the בעיא in favor of the festival-need approach.

phrases.aramaic: מְקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ — אִין, לֹא נָהֲגוּ — לָא,
phrases.english: A place where they are accustomed, yes; where they are not accustomed, no.
And learn from it:
for the needs of the festival, yes;
not for the needs of the festival, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ — אִין, לֹא נָהֲגוּ — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes רבי מאיר's ברייתא from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the line on ערב פסח depends on whether the work is for the festival.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of רבי מאיר's ברייתא, including the custom clause.

steps.title: Conclusion: the proof stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof from רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof and closes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first proof, this one is not rejected. The question about work on ערב פסח is answered: festival work is allowed and non-festival work is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר's ברייתא, the line on ערב פסח depends on whether the work is for the festival. The first ברייתא was rejected as a proof because it may only be teaching finishing versus starting.

phrases.english: Learn from it (indeed, that is so).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the inference of step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Work for the festival is allowed on ערב פסח, and work that is not for the festival is not.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the חכמים allow three crafts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, where the חכמים say only three crafts may work on ערב פסח until midday.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: three crafts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to explain it. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step, which names the three crafts and gives the reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say which three crafts it means or why. The גמרא now turns to a ברייתא to fill that in.

phrases.english: And the Sages say: three crafts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בעיא and returns to explaining the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only three crafts may work on ערב פסח until midday.

steps.title: Which three crafts, and why: tailors, barbers, launderers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא names tailors, barbers, and launderers. Each is allowed because the same work is allowed in some form on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: tailors, because an ordinary person may sew in his normal way on חול המועד. Barbers and launderers, because someone arriving from overseas or leaving prison may cut hair and wash clothes on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא names the three crafts from the משנה. It explains each one by pointing to a similar permission on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is: if this work is allowed on חול המועד, where work is treated more strictly, it can be allowed on ערב פסח. Tailoring is allowed outright for an ordinary person. Haircuts and laundry are allowed for people who could not do them before the festival.

keyTerms.meaning: an ordinary person, not a professional
the intermediate days of the festival

phrases.english: It was taught: Tailors,
since an ordinary person may sew in his normal way
on the intermediate days of the festival.
Barbers and launderers,
since one who arrives from overseas
and one who leaves prison
may cut hair and launder on the intermediate days of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which three crafts the משנה means.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tailors, barbers, and launderers may work on ערב פסח, because similar work is allowed on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds shoemakers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds shoemakers, because pilgrims may repair their shoes on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: shoemakers too, because pilgrims coming for the festival may repair their shoes on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא adds a fourth craft to the list, using the same kind of reasoning from חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On חול המועד only shoe repair, which is finishing work, is allowed. Yet רבי יוסי allows shoemakers on ערב פסח to do their full job, including making new shoes. This sets up the question of what exactly he and the חכמים disagree about.

keyTerms.meaning: pilgrims going up to ירושלים for the festival

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
Also the shoemakers,
since festival pilgrims may repair their shoes
on the intermediate days of the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הָרַצְעָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth craft to the ברייתא's list of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shoemakers may also work on ערב פסח.

steps.title: What is the disagreement about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle lies behind the argument between the חכמים and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the underlying reason behind the disagreement. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same method of learning from חול המועד, yet they disagree about shoemakers. The גמרא wants to find the exact point where they part ways.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the disagreement in steps 8 and 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that separates the חכמים from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: Can we learn starting work from finishing work?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that we learn the rule for starting work from the rule for finishing work. The חכמים hold that we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: we learn the start of work from the end of work. And one master holds: we do not learn the start of work from the end of work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument depends on one principle: whether permission to finish work (repairing shoes) can teach permission to start work (making new shoes).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shoe repair on חול המועד is only finishing work. רבי יוסי reasons from it that making shoes from scratch is allowed on ערב פסח. The חכמים say starting is different, so shoemakers are not on their list. Tailors are on the list because on חול המועד an ordinary person sews fully, not just repairs.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: we learn starting work from finishing work, so shoemakers may work. חכמים: we do not, so only tailors, barbers, and launderers may work.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that starting and finishing work are different runs through this whole sugya. It appeared earlier with 'finishing yes, starting no,' and it returns here to explain the argument about crafts.

phrases.english: One master holds:
we learn the beginning of work from the end of work;
and one master holds:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְמֵידִין תְּחִילַּת מְלָאכָה מִסּוֹף מְלָאכָה.
phrases.english: we do not learn the beginning of work from the end of work.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: לְמֵידִין תְּחִילַּת מְלָאכָה מִסּוֹף מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether permission to finish work (shoe repair) teaches permission to start work (making new shoes).

steps.title: New משנה: Chickens, Animal Dung, and Repaired Vessels
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists more tasks that are allowed on ערב פסח, and some that are allowed on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the fourteenth of ניסן you may set chickens to sit on eggs. If a sitting hen ran away, you may put it back. If it died, you may put another hen in its place. On the fourteenth you may sweep dung from under an animal's feet. On חול המועד you may only push the dung to the sides. You may take vessels to a craftsman and bring them back, even if they are not needed for the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists more jobs that are allowed on ערב פסח, the fourteenth of ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting a hen on eggs from the start is allowed on the fourteenth. Returning a runaway hen, or replacing one that died, protects eggs that are already being incubated. Sweeping dung away fully is allowed on the fourteenth, but on חול המועד you may only push it aside, which is less work.

keyTerms.meaning: Brooding nests, meaning hens set to sit on eggs
The fourteenth of ניסן, ערב פסח
Push aside, which is a lighter action

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מוֹשִׁיבִין שׁוֹבָכִין לְתַרְנְגוֹלִים בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר.
phrases.english: MISHNA: One may set brooding nests for hens on the fourteenth.
phrases.notes: This means placing a hen on eggs so they will hatch.

phrases.english: And a hen that ran away, one may return it to its place,
and if it died, one may set another in its place.

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹרְפִין מִתַּחַת רַגְלֵי בְּהֵמָה בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר,
phrases.english: One may sweep dung from under an animal's feet on the fourteenth,
and on the festival's middle days one pushes it to the sides.
One may take vessels to the craftsman's house and bring them back,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָם לְצוֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.english: even though they are not needed for the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מוֹשִׁיבִין שׁוֹבָכִין לְתַרְנְגוֹלִים בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of crafts on ערב פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting hens on eggs, returning or replacing a hen, sweeping dung, and moving vessels to and from a craftsman are all allowed on the fourteenth. On חול המועד, dung may only be pushed aside.

steps.title: Why Mention Returning the Hen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say a hen may be returned, since setting a hen on eggs from the start is already allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if we may even set a hen on eggs from the start, do we really need to be told that we may return it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that part of the משנה seems unnecessary. If starting fresh is allowed, returning a hen is surely allowed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is: the bigger action is allowed, so the smaller action should be obvious. A משנה does not usually say obvious things, so this clause needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if already. This opens a 'surely this is obvious' argument.
We may set a hen down from the start
Do we need to be told about returning it?

phrases.english: GEMARA: Now, if we may even set a hen down from the start,
is it necessary to say we may return it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges an apparently extra clause in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause allowing a runaway hen to be returned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bigger action of setting a hen from the start is allowed, the smaller action of returning it is obvious, so the clause seems unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: That Clause Is About חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the clause about returning the hen refers to חול המועד, when setting a new hen is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The later part of the משנה is talking about חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by saying the משנה has switched topics. It is now talking about חול המועד, not the fourteenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On חול המועד you may not set a hen on eggs from the start. You may still return a runaway hen, because otherwise the eggs would be lost. So the clause is not obvious. It teaches a separate rule for a different time.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה
We have arrived at a new topic
The middle days of the festival

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the whole משנה as being about ערב פסח. According to אביי, the clause about returning the hen is about חול המועד, so רב הונא's limits in the next step apply to חול המועד.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
In the latter clause we have arrived at the intermediate festival days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לְחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the extra clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-locating the clause to a different time (חול המועד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה is about the fourteenth, so returning a hen is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clause about returning the hen is about חול המועד, when only returning a hen is allowed, not setting a new one.

steps.title: רב הונא Limits When the Hen May Be Returned
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says a hen may be returned only if it ran away within the last three days and had already sat on the eggs for three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: This was taught only if it is within three days of the hen running away, because its body heat has not yet gone. It must also be after three days of sitting, because then the eggs would be completely ruined. But if more than three days passed since it ran away, the heat is gone. And if it sat less than three days, the eggs are not yet completely ruined. In those cases we do not return it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא sets two conditions for returning the hen on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the hen must have run away less than three days ago. After that it has cooled off and will not go back to sitting, so returning it is useless. Second, it must have sat at least three days. Before that, the eggs can still be sold as food, so leaving them causes only a small loss.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of. This phrase limits a rule.
Its rebellion, meaning the hen running away
Heat, the hen's warmth for brooding

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: They taught this only
within three days of its running away,
because the heat has not yet left it,
and after three days of its sitting,
because the eggs would be completely ruined.
But after three days of its running away,
when its heat has left it,
or within three days of its sitting,
when the eggs are not yet completely ruined,
we do not return it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא תּוֹךְ שְׁלֹשָׁה לְמִרְדָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's rule on returning a hen, as אביי explained it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Returning the hen is allowed only within three days of its running away, and only after it has sat at least three days.

steps.title: רבי אמי: Return It Even in the First Three Days
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי disagrees and allows returning the hen even if it sat less than three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Even within three days of its sitting, we return it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי argues with one of רב הונא's two conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי allows returning the hen even when the eggs are not yet completely ruined. He does not argue about the first condition. A hen that has already cooled off is useless to return.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Even within three days of its sitting, we return it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תּוֹךְ שְׁלֹשָׁה לִישִׁיבָתָהּ מַהְדְּרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רב הונא's second condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hen may be returned even if it sat on the eggs less than three days.

steps.title: What Is the Root of Their Argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רב הונא and רבי אמי disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the argument. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants the general principle that leads each one to his position, not just their two rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: About what principle do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the principle behind the argument between רב הונא and רבי אמי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that separates רב הונא and רבי אמי

steps.title: Big Loss Versus Small Loss
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds the חכמים worried only about a big loss. רבי אמי holds they worried about a small loss too.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: they were concerned about a big loss, but not about a small loss. The other master holds: they were concerned about a small loss too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the argument is about how much loss justifies work on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eggs sat on for less than three days can still be sold, but for less money. That is a small loss. רב הונא says that is not enough to permit returning the hen. רבי אמי says even a small loss is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: They were concerned about, meaning the חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: On חול המועד, work to prevent loss is sometimes allowed. רב הונא allows it only to prevent a big loss. רבי אמי allows it even to prevent a small loss.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of הפסד מרובה versus הפסד מועט comes up throughout the laws of חול המועד. It decides how much loss is needed to permit work.

phrases.english: One master holds: about a big loss they were concerned,
about a small loss they were not concerned,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לְהֶפְסֵד מוּעָט נָמֵי חָשְׁשׁוּ.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: about a small loss they were also concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the root of the argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא: the חכמים permitted work only to prevent a big loss. רבי אמי: they permitted it even to prevent a small loss.

steps.title: A ברייתא about clearing dung
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'גורפין מתחת' and brings a ברייתא with more detail about dung in a courtyard and a barn.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may sweep from beneath the animals.' The רבנן taught: Dung in a courtyard may be moved to the sides. Dung in a barn and in a courtyard may be taken out to the garbage dump.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה, about sweeping dung, and quotes a ברייתא that gives more detail. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two rules. Dung in a courtyard is only pushed to the sides. Dung in 'a barn and a courtyard' is taken all the way out to the dump. These two rules seem to clash, and that clash is the next step.

phrases.english: One may sweep from beneath (the animals).
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. It is the heading for this new topic.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The dung in the courtyard, one moves it to the sides,
(dung) that is in the barn and in the courtyard,
one takes it out to the garbage dump.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַזֶּבֶל שֶׁבֶּחָצֵר מְסַלְּקִין אוֹתוֹ לִצְדָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה (sweeping dung), after the discussion about hens ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Courtyard dung is moved to the sides. Barn and courtyard dung is taken out to the dump.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא first allows only moving courtyard dung to the sides, and then allows taking courtyard dung out to the dump.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult! You said that courtyard dung is moved only to the sides. Then it teaches that dung in the barn and the courtyard is taken out to the dump!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two halves of the ברייתא seem to clash with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half implies that courtyard dung may NOT go to the dump, only to the sides. The second half says that courtyard dung DOES go to the dump. The same place gets two different rules.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult. Used when a source contradicts itself.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult,
you said: dung in the courtyard
one moves it to the sides,
phrases.notes: This implies: only to the sides, not to the dump.

phrases.english: and then it teaches: (dung) in the barn and in the courtyard
one takes it out to the dump!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא quoted in step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first half limits courtyard dung to the sides, but the second half lets courtyard dung go to the dump. These cannot both be true for the same case.

steps.title: אביי: two different days
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that one rule is for the fourteenth of ניסן and the other is for חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. Here it is talking about the fourteenth, and there it is talking about חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי solves the contradiction by saying that each half of the ברייתא is about a different time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב פסח (the fourteenth), more work is allowed, so the dung may be taken out to the dump. On חול המועד, work is more limited, so it is only moved to the sides. So the two halves never apply to the same day.

keyTerms.meaning: The fourteenth of ניסן, ערב פסח
The intermediate days of the festival

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult,
here it is on the fourteenth,
phrases.notes: Taking it out to the dump is allowed on the fourteenth.

phrases.english: there it is on the intermediate days of the festival.
phrases.notes: Only moving it to the sides is allowed on חול המועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by time (ערב פסח versus חול המועד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both halves of the ברייתא are about the same day, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dump is allowed on the fourteenth. Only the sides are allowed on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבא: both are חול המועד, depending on how dirty the courtyard is
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both halves are about חול המועד. If the courtyard became as dirty as a barn, the dung may be taken out to the dump.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Both this and that are about חול המועד. This is what it means: if the courtyard has become like a barn, one takes the dung out to the dump.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the same contradiction. He keeps both halves on the same day and splits them by the condition of the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal courtyard with a little dung: only move the dung to the sides. A courtyard so full of dung that it looks like a barn: it may be cleared out to the dump, even on חול המועד. The word 'barn' in the ברייתא describes how dirty the courtyard is, not a separate place.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that, meaning both cases
And this is what it means. Used to reread a source.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying that every courtyard may be cleared to the dump. Only a courtyard that has become as filthy as a barn may be cleared that way.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: הָא וְהָא בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד,
phrases.english: Rava said: This and that are on the intermediate days,
and this is what it is saying:
if the courtyard has become like a barn —
one takes it out to the garbage dump.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָא וְהָא בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 20 that disagrees with אביי's split by time.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא: both halves are on the same day, but they describe different conditions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Barn and courtyard' means a separate place, so it clashes with the first half.
steps.terutzMaskana: On חול המועד, a courtyard as dirty as a barn may be cleared to the dump. A normal courtyard may only be cleared to the sides.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: אביי splits by day (fourteenth versus חול המועד). רבא keeps both on חול המועד and splits by how dirty the courtyard is.

steps.title: רב פפא recalls רבא's test about vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about vessels at a craftsman. רב פפא says רבא tested them on it, starting with the משנה's ruling that this is allowed even if the vessels are not needed for the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may take vessels to the craftsman and bring them back.' רב פפא said: רבא tested us. We learned: one may take and bring vessels from the craftsman's house, even if they are not needed for the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next part of the משנה. רב פפא sets up a test that רבא once gave his students, and the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source being tested is a משנה that allows moving vessels to and from a craftsman even when they are not needed for the festival. That is a lenient rule. It is the starting point that the next source will seem to contradict.

phrases.english: One may take vessels and bring from the craftsman's house.
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה. It is the heading for this new topic.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בָּדֵיק לַן רָבָא.
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Rava tested us.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: מוֹלִיכִין וּמְבִיאִין כֵּלִים מִבֵּית הָאוּמָּן,
phrases.english: We learned: one may take and bring vessels from the craftsman's house,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָן לְצוֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.english: even though they are not for the needs of the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בָּדֵיק לַן רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, after the dung discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessels may be taken to and from a craftsman even when they are not needed for the festival.

steps.title: Another source forbids bringing vessels from the craftsman
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a contradicting source: vessels may not be brought from the craftsman, and if he fears theft he may only move them to another courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he contrasted it with this: One may not bring vessels from the craftsman's house. If he is worried they might be stolen, he moves them to a different courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רבא's actual test. He shows a source that says the opposite of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows bringing vessels home from the craftsman. This source forbids it. It only allows the owner to move them to another courtyard for safety, not home. So one source permits and the other forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: And he contrasted them. Introduces a contradicting source.

phrases.english: And he contrasted them:
one may not bring vessels from the craftsman's house,
and if he is worried about them that they may be stolen —
he moves them to another courtyard!
phrases.notes: Not to his own house, only to a safer spot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the משנה quoted in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה in step 23 that allows bringing vessels from the craftsman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One source allows bringing vessels home. The other forbids it and only allows moving them to another courtyard.

steps.title: First answer: ערב פסח versus חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The students answered that the משנה is about the fourteenth, and the forbidding source is about חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we answered: It is not difficult. Here it is the fourteenth, and there it is חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tells the first answer he and his friends gave to רבא's test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same kind of split that אביי used for the dung. On ערב פסח, bringing vessels home is allowed. On חול המועד, it is forbidden, and the owner may only move them to a safer courtyard.

phrases.english: And we answered: It is not difficult:
here — on the fourteenth,
phrases.notes: Our משנה, where bringing vessels is allowed.

phrases.english: there — on the intermediate days.
phrases.notes: This is the source that forbids it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources are about the same day.
steps.terutzMaskana: Allowed on the fourteenth. Forbidden on חול המועד.

steps.title: Second answer: does he trust the craftsman?
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, both sources are about חול המועד. If the owner trusts the craftsman, he may not bring the vessels home. If he does not trust him, he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: both this and that are about חול המועד, and it is not difficult. Here it is when he trusts him, and there it is when he does not trust him.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer keeps both sources on חול המועד and splits them by whether the owner trusts the craftsman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner trusts the craftsman, the vessels are safe where they are, so there is no reason to allow bringing them home. If he does not trust him, he is afraid of losing them, so he is allowed to bring them home. This matches the earlier idea that the חכמים allowed things in order to prevent a loss.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say. Introduces another answer.

steps.confusionAlert: The forbidding source is the case where he DOES trust the craftsman. Trust means there is no need to rush the vessels home.
steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions here get two kinds of answers. One answer splits by day (ערב פסח versus חול המועד). The other keeps both on חול המועד and splits by the situation (how dirty the courtyard is, or whether he trusts the craftsman). For the vessels, though, this trust answer does not survive: step 28 challenges it, and step 29 returns to the split by day.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: הָא וְהָא בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: this and that are on the intermediate days, and it is not difficult:
here — when he trusts him,
phrases.notes: This is the source that forbids it: he has no need to bring the vessels home.

phrases.english: there — when he does not trust him.
phrases.notes: Our משנה: he may bring the vessels home.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, הָא וְהָא בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 24, as an alternative to step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by situation (trust in the craftsman), with both sources on the same day
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources are about the same situation on חול המועד.
steps.terutzMaskana: If he trusts the craftsman, he may not bring the vessels home. If he does not trust him, he may.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rules of חול המועד bend to prevent a real fear of loss, the same idea seen in the hen discussion.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the trust distinction
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if the owner does not trust the craftsman, or fears theft, he may move the vessels or even bring them home quietly on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One may bring vessels from a craftsman's house, such as a jug from a potter or a cup from a glassmaker. But one may not bring wool from a dyer, or other vessels from a craftsman. If the craftsman has nothing to eat, the owner pays him and leaves the item with him. If the owner does not trust him, he moves the items to a house near the craftsman. If he fears they will be stolen, he brings them quietly into his own house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to back up the second answer from Step 26. That answer said the rule depends on whether the owner trusts the craftsman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows vessels needed for the festival, like a jug or a cup, but forbids ordinary items. Its ending is the key part: when the owner does not trust the craftsman or fears theft, it gets easier for him to move the vessels. This matches the idea that 'no trust' allows him to bring them home.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (here it introduces a supporting ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: Here וְהָתַנְיָא is not an attack. It means 'and so it was taught,' and it brings support for the previous answer.

phrases.english: As it was taught: One may bring vessels from the house of a craftsman,
such as a jug from the potter's house,
or a cup from the glassmaker's house.
But not wool from the dyer's house,
phrases.notes: Wool is not needed for the festival.

phrases.english: and not other vessels from the craftsman's house,
phrases.notes: Vessels that are not needed for the festival.

phrases.english: And if the craftsman has nothing to eat,
he gives him his pay and leaves the item with him.
And if he does not trust him,
he leaves them in a house next to him.
And if he worries they may be stolen,
he brings them quietly into his house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 26's distinction between trusting and not trusting the craftsman.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that, on חול המועד, bringing vessels home depends on whether the owner trusts the craftsman.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that allows moving the vessels when the owner does not trust the craftsman, and bringing them home quietly when he fears theft.

steps.title: The trust answer cannot explain taking vessels to the craftsman
steps.stepSummary: The trust answer explains 'bringing' vessels home. But the משנה also allows 'taking' vessels to the craftsman, and the ברייתא forbids that even more strongly.
steps.simpleTranslation: You explained 'bringing.' But 'taking' is still a problem, because the ברייתא taught: one may not bring, and all the more so one may not take.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second answer from Step 26. It shows that the answer only covers half of the משנה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows both taking vessels to the craftsman and bringing them back. The trust idea can explain bringing them home, since he worries about the vessels. But taking a vessel to be repaired has nothing to do with trust, and the ברייתא forbids it with a קל וחומר: if bringing is forbidden, taking is surely forbidden.

phrases.english: You have explained 'bringing.'
'Taking' is still a difficulty,
since it teaches: one may not bring,
and all the more so one may not take!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the alternative answer given in Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that both sources are about חול המועד and differ only by whether the owner trusts the craftsman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows taking vessels to the craftsman as well. The trust distinction cannot explain that, and the forbidding ברייתא rules out taking even more strongly than bringing.

steps.title: Back to the first answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the trust answer and accepts the first answer: the משנה is about ערב פסח, and the forbidding ברייתא is about חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear as we answered at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the first answer from Step 25 is the correct one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the trust answer failed, the only answer left is the time-based one. On ערב פסח (the fourteenth), one may both take and bring vessels. On חול המועד, one may not.
steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: the משנה allowing vessels to go to and from a craftsman is about ערב פסח. On חול המועד this is forbidden, except in the special cases the ברייתא mentions, like fear of theft.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
as we answered at the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 26 because of Step 28 and returns to Step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is about the fourteenth (ערב פסח). The ברייתא that forbids it is about חול המועד.

steps.title: Six practices of the people of יריחו; three the חכמים did not protest
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the people of יריחו did six unusual things. The חכמים protested three of them and did not protest the other three. The three not protested were grafting palms all day on the fourteenth, 'bundling' שמע, and harvesting and piling grain before the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of יריחו did six things. The חכמים protested three and did not protest three. These are the ones they did not protest: they grafted palm trees all day long on the fourteenth; they 'bundled' שמע; and they harvested and piled grain before the עומר was brought.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists unusual customs of the people of יריחו, starting with the three the חכמים let them keep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה connects to the earlier topic of working on ערב פסח: grafting palms 'all day' means even after midday on the fourteenth. 'Bundling שמע' will be explained in the גמרא on the next amud. Harvesting and piling grain before the עומר is normally a problem, and the גמרא on the next amud discusses why the חכמים did not protest it.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן, which permits the new grain

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not protested' does not always mean the חכמים fully agreed. It means they did not stop the people from doing it.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים עָשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי יְרִיחוֹ,
phrases.english: MISHNA: Six things the people of Jericho did,
on three they protested against them,
and on three they did not protest against them.
And these are the ones they did not protest:
they grafted palm trees all day long,
phrases.notes: All day on the fourteenth of ניסן, even after midday.

phrases.english: and they 'bundled' שמע,
and they harvested and piled grain before the עומר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people of יריחו had six customs. The חכמים did not protest three of them: grafting palms all day on the fourteenth, bundling שמע, and harvesting and piling before the עומר.

steps.title: The protested practices begin: using branches of הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts listing the three practices the חכמים protested. The first is permitting the use of branches that grew from הקדש trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the ones they protested: they permitted the use of branches of הקדש trees.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the second list, the three practices the חכמים protested. The rest of the list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These were carob or sycamore trees whose branches had been cut and dedicated to the מקדש, and then new branches grew. The people of יריחו treated the new growth as ordinary and permitted it. The חכמים protested, because the new growth still counted as הקדש.

phrases.english: And these are the ones they protested:
they permitted branches of הקדש,
phrases.notes: New branches that grew from dedicated trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from the practices not protested to those that were protested.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים protested when the people of יריחו permitted the use of branches that grew from הקדש trees.
